automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Include only public items published or visibly updated inside the exact two-day window. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, and boundary-only dates.

searched_topics: identity, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, runtime, cloud, and deployment supply chains
security evaluation, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, governance, regulation, and audit evidence
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned

methods: NVD CVE API keyword searches for AI, MCP, agent, model, prompt, LLM, and OpenShift AI within the publication and last-modified window

qualifying_findings.title: knowns MCP tool path traversal permits file access outside the project directory
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: knowns versions before 0.30.0 did not validate filesystem paths in MCP tool arguments. A caller could use traversal sequences to read, create, overwrite, or delete Markdown files outside the project directory that were accessible to the server process.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record plus NVD entry, vendor GitHub security advisory, patch commit, and release notes
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: knowns npm package before 0.30.0; MCP doc and memory tools; CWE-22; CVSS 3.1 8.8 HIGH in NVD
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP servers commonly mediate agent file access. A path-containment failure lets an agent-facing tool cross the project boundary and turns delegated document or memory access into arbitrary local file manipulation.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Owns the MCP tool path-containment and agent filesystem boundary implication.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Owns any broad knowns or MCP-server catalog page if durable ecosystem coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: May own general project-memory or documentation-agent workflow practice; do not duplicate here.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct CVE, NVD, vendor advisory, commit, and release references all align inside the run window.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, check whether a local knowns MCP path-containment leaf already exists before creating a new one.
Reconcile v0.30.0 release notes and vendor advisory wording for exact fixed-version language.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenShift AI dashboard exposes NVIDIA NGC and NIM pull secrets without authorization
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The odh-dashboard backend-for-frontend route GET /api/nim-serving/:nimResource in Red Hat OpenShift AI reads Kubernetes Secrets using the dashboard service account and returns full Secret objects, including .data, without an authorization check. Any authenticated dashboard user can retrieve the cluster NVIDIA NGC API key Secret and NIM image pull secret.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Red Hat CNA CVE record plus NVD entry and Red Hat security references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Red Hat OpenShift AI / odh-dashboard packages listed in the CVE record; missing authorization CWE-862 and insufficiently protected credentials CWE-522; NVD CVSS 3.1 6.5 MEDIUM
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The issue exposes AI platform credentials used for NVIDIA NGC and NIM model-serving image access, directly affecting model-serving supply chain access control and least-privilege boundaries.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Owns the AI platform credential disclosure and missing authorization analysis.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Owns broad Red Hat, OpenShift AI, NVIDIA NGC, or NIM entity context.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: May own development-platform governance practices only if a downstream practice source appears.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: direct Red Hat CVE record and NVD entry name the affected AI platform, route, credentials, and authorization failure.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, map this to identity-and-access and data-and-privacy pages as appropriate.
Recheck Red Hat advisory access for fixed package state and remediation wording.

qualifying_findings.title: ModelCloud GPTQModel Triton dequantization kernel has out-of-bounds read
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: ModelCloud GPTQModel through 7.2.0 has an out-of-bounds read in gptqmodel/nn_modules/qlinear/tritonv2.py in the Triton dequantization kernel through manipulation of g_idx. The CVE states public exploit disclosure and recommends upgrading to 7.3.0, with patch commit 877c732f7d7dccd56a729844c6a5bd20f3aa8bb1.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE record and NVD entry with VulDB advisory, public issue, pull request, patch commit, and release tag
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ModelCloud GPTQModel versions 7.0, 7.1, and 7.2.0 affected; 7.3.0 unaffected; Triton dequantization kernel; CWE-125/CWE-119
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Quantized model runtimes and kernels are part of AI deployment supply chains. Memory-safety flaws in model execution code can affect systems that load or serve optimized model artifacts.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Owns the model-runtime memory-safety and deployment supply-chain implication.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Owns broad GPTQModel/model-compression entity context if needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: No direct local development-practice routing identified.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence: CVE, NVD, issue, PR, commit, and release are present; VulDB wording says public exploit disclosure but ingest should inspect issue/PR details before durable prose.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, verify the GitHub issue and patch diff for whether the flaw is reachable through untrusted model inputs, remote service inputs, or only local API misuse.

qualifying_findings.title: Igniter package-install confirmation prompt can be forged by malicious package metadata
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: ash-project igniter versions from 0.8.1 before 0.8.4 allow a malicious package publisher to embed ANSI terminal escape sequences in package metadata shown by mix igniter.install. The confirmation panel can be overwritten to forge trusted author names or download counts and hide the real package metadata, deceiving a developer into approving a malicious dependency.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE record and NVD entry with vendor GitHub security advisory, CNA page, OSV entry, and patch commit
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Igniter participates in framework and dependency setup workflows. The issue weakens anti-typosquatting approval UI, a relevant supply-chain control for agent-assisted or AI-accelerated dependency installation.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Owns package-install trust UI and AI-assisted dependency approval implications.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Owns broad framework/tool entity context only if durable ecosystem coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: May own general developer workflow approval and dependency-vetting practice.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for vulnerability and fixed version; AI-specificity is indirect but relevant to supply-chain approval boundaries used by agent-assisted development workflows.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, route broad developer-workflow practice to ai-dev-wiki and keep only the supply-chain security approval implication here.

qualifying_findings.title: SureForms AI Forms WordPress plugin has unauthenticated stored XSS
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The SureForms - Contact Form Builder, AI Forms, Payment Form, Survey & Quiz WordPress plugin through 2.12.2 is vulnerable to unauthenticated stored cross-site scripting via text-field entity-encoded payloads because of insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. WordPress Trac references show changes for 2.12.3.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Wordfence CNA CVE record and NVD entry with Wordfence threat-intel reference and WordPress Trac code-change references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: SureForms WordPress plugin up to and including 2.12.2; fixed changes in 2.12.3 references; CWE-79
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI-enabled form plugins can collect user prompts, survey data, and contact/payment workflow data. Stored XSS in that surface can compromise users or administrative sessions and can become a prompt/data contamination path for AI-assisted form workflows.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Owns broad product/provider context for SureForms or Brainstorm Force if needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: No direct local development-practice routing identified.
